title: Pouring beans
offscreen: It's already a hands-on activity: repeat it over the following days without presenting it again; the child chooses it on their own.

materials.label: A handful of beans or chickpeas

steps.text: Carry the tray to the table with two hands, slowly.
Pick up the full bowl with two hands and pour into the other one, slowly, without talking.
Look: has a bean fallen out? Pick it up with two fingers and put it in the bowl.
Now pour the beans back into the first bowl. Repeat as many times as you like.
Take the tray back to where you found it.

levels.control: The beans that fell onto the tray show by themselves whether the pouring went well: the grown-up doesn't need to say so.
levels.observe: How many times they repeat it, whether they use two hands, whether they pick up fallen beans without being asked.

intro.bo: {nome}, this one is done with your hands, not on the tablet. Call a grown-up and I'll watch you.
intro.pilu: {nome}, you need real objects for this one. A grown-up shows you once, then it's your turn.
intro.tango: {nome}! Real work! Call a grown-up: first you watch, then you do it. I won't touch anything, promise.

outro.bo: You worked on your own, {nome}. Let's put everything away, so you'll find it again tomorrow.
outro.pilu: Everything goes back in its place, {nome}: that's part of the work. See you tomorrow.
outro.tango: Done! {nome}, shall we put everything away? I'll... I'll watch. See you tomorrow!
